cells.tense: You are still at the practice, and the hoping has not run out from under it.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Carry the practice on your own say-so. No tally, no one to report to. Do it at the usual time and let how it goes stand as the whole record of it.
cells.core:
The small light in your practice is still lit. It runs the plain way — attention, return, day after day — and the appetite behind it hasn't thinned. That is the grown shape of this: not a burst that somehow survived, but hoping that kept its edge through everything and is still doing the work. At the practice, the hope and the labour sit together without friction.

What this balance is free to feed next is your own hold on it. Pick the practice you most want to last and carry it off your own reserves — no outside prompts, nobody to answer to, just the return you make yourself. Nothing has to fail for this to be worth doing. It is how the thing stays yours, and how the hope underneath it simply continues.
cells.sheetLine: The light is still on, and it is still yours.
cells.verb: keeping on toward a thing you chose, long after the choosing
cells.place: the one practice you keep at, alone, over and over

cells.tense: You will keep this going, and you are already braced for the day it goes badly.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Hold two true things about the practice at once and declare neither. Put both on a page, then close it. Say nothing until they settle.
cells.core:
You are pushing the practice forward faster than it can carry you. Hoping has turned into a vigil — waiting to find out whether it is working, weighing each day against a finish line nobody set, bracing for the failure you may have to survive. Readiness has become the whole posture, and the practice gets done inside that grip. On a good day the shine is real; here it runs ahead of what has actually been built.

So let one certainty wait. Hold two true things about this at once — the case that it is working and the case that it isn't — down on one page, and declare neither. Close the page. Not-knowing gets more comfortable the more you practise it, and you get to stop having judged it before the week is out.

cells.tense: You stood at the beginning of the practice and something in it never got taken up.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Take one small corner of the practice and tend just that, by hand, on your own timetable. Make it the one you actually touch.
cells.core:
The practice goes through its motions and finishes nothing. You come to it from behind — half-arrived, doing it at the edges of the hour — and what gets made is thin, unconvincing, not yet solid enough to stand on. The hope has no traction, because there is nothing underneath it that says the wait was worth it. Standing there is not a character flaw; it is a small thing left untended so long it stopped pulling.

So tend something small enough to look after properly. Take one line, one rep, one corner of the practice and give it a steady hand on your own schedule — not the whole craft, just that. What grows under care that isn't clutching tends to continue. Start with the smallest piece; the larger shape can follow when it follows.

cells.tense: Through material pressure you are still standing, and the standing has been filed as stubbornness.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: Stay where you are through the next pressure, and know it is you doing the staying. No announcement, nobody to tell. Then carry on as before.
cells.core:
There is a way you hold under weight — patient, unmoved, a refusal to fold that has been doing the work for a while now. Ask you and you would probably say it is just hanging in there, the situation being what it is, no special credit due. But the strength is the same one you draw on at the practice, and the situation doesn't own it.

Pause at the next thing you quietly outlast. Catch yourself in the moment of staying and know that you are the one doing it, then carry on. Nothing needs to be proved and nobody needs to hear it. The only difference between being a bystander to your own endurance and owning it is that the owner knows.
cells.sheetLine: The staying has been yours, not the situation's.

attempts.check: The record gives Resilience as abundant persistence through aspiration, tested and still standing — it does not say who left, how long the hardship lasted, or what the person learned in it, so all four cells must name the standing and never the history. The likely objection is 'this doesn't feel like abundance, it feels like I'm worn thin' — which is exactly why the Too Little and Too Much cells name the wear without arguing with it. The asks survive a wrong read: each is one small act of the medicine (persist on your own reserves, weigh what you know, tend the resource, pause and know), useful whether or not the diagnosis is true, and none depends on money, energy, a witness, or a good week. The sentence that serves me more than the person is the one that would make the persistence sound noble; I've kept the disciplines plain and local and cut anything that flatters.
